channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Seabirds See Miracle Recovery After Avian Flu Wiped Them Out
item.description: Sandwich terns wiped out by bird flu three years ago have rebuilt a colony on England's south coast, now 756 strong. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Keep dogs on a lead near nesting beaches in spring and summer. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm to open to the public: ‘This land shaped him and his legacy’
item.description: Jimmy Carter's family farm in Georgia has been bought for permanent protection and will open to the public. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers raised more than $76,000 for a caregiver after a doorbell video of her kindness spread. How you can help: Tell a carer in your life what their work means to you. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World’s Driest Desert Erupts into Record-Breaking Bloom Boom (LOOK)
item.description: Chile's Atacama, the driest desert on Earth, has burst into its largest recorded bloom, with about 200 species. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Actor, 85, takes to the stage despite Alzheimer’s diagnosis
item.description: An 85-year-old actor living with Alzheimer's is back on stage in Beckett's Krapp's Last Tape. Source: Positive News.

item.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
item.description: After a 40-year search, CERN found evidence of a particle decay that happens about once in 10 billion. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric ferries that lift above the water are arriving in US cities, offering quieter, cleaner crossings. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Take the ferry, train or bus instead of driving when one serves your route. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
item.description: Researchers traced a gut-to-brain dopamine path that explains how we learn to enjoy bitter tastes like coffee. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Man’s Halloween Skeletons Prove Perfect Treat to Woman Battling Breast Cancer
item.description: A man's skeleton displays, once met with hate mail, now cheer a woman on her weekly drive to cancer treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: US colleges are adding childcare, family spaces and flexible support so students with children can finish. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Interpreting Autistic Cues Is Difficult, a Teen Built an App That’s Helping Hundreds of Families
item.description: A teen taught himself machine learning and built an app that helps 700 families read autistic cues. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Fish Stocks Thrive Thanks to This Pink Seaweed and Locals Who Protected It
item.description: Ten years after a dredging ban, pink maerl seaweed beds off a Scottish island are thriving and fish are back. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Choose scallops labelled as diver-caught rather than dredged. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Glowworms Shine Again in the UK from Larvae Reared Pro Bono in Garden Shed
item.description: A volunteer breeds glowworms in his garden shed and releases the larvae, bringing their light back to UK sites. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Leave a patch of your garden unlit and uncut so glowworms and other insects can thrive. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A UCLA study found a natural molecule eased brain fog and tiredness in breast cancer survivors. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon
item.description: Sticky marine snow can carry six times more carbon to the deep ocean, a natural climate ally scientists now understand. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: Fossils in Colombia reveal a rich ancient sea of giant reptiles and sharks, reshaping ideas about evolution. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dogs Can Sniff-Out Invasive Plant Species With High Accuracy to Curb Their Destruction
item.description: Trained dogs in Germany found invasive plants with high accuracy, helping catch them before they spread. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Lucky Bird Found in Storm Drain a Mile From Home After Passing Driver Happens to Spot it Hopping in
item.description: A pet budgie blown out of a window in a storm was found safe in a drain a mile away by a passing driver. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Let a thousand blossoms bloom: Sydney’s jacarandas put on their spring show – in pictures
item.description: Sydney's jacaranda trees are in full purple bloom for spring, carpeting streets in flowers. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Baby Saved After Racing Heartbeat Detected by Family Doberman
item.description: A family Doberman's restless worry led to a six-month-old's racing heart being found and treated in time. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Adventurer Finally Hugs Mom After 28-Year Walk Around the World From Home in UK
item.description: After a 28-year, 31,000-mile walk around the world, Karl Bushby is home in Hull with his mother. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
item.description: Europe was long open woodland and meadow grazed by large animals, a finding that can guide how land is restored. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
item.description: The Rubin Observatory found two unknown companions of the Milky Way after scanning only 7% of the sky. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: People Around the World Help Buy Royal Estate for Wildlife Conservation
item.description: Donors around the world pooled millions to buy an estate where curlews, lapwings and rare bumblebees live. How you can help: Join or volunteer with a local nature reserve or land trust near you. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Spends 12 Days Returning Lost Cash a Laborer Needed for His Daughter
item.description: A man in southern Brazil spent 12 days tracing a labourer to return the savings he had dropped. How you can help: If you find lost cash, hand it to the police or the venue so it can reach its owner. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Venomous Primate Believed Extinct for 100 Years Was Hiding in Plain Sight All Along
item.description: The Bangka slow loris, once feared extinct, has been filmed alive and well thanks to a local wildlife group. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Geothermal Utilities Power Wave of US Affordable Housing with 40% Energy Savings
item.description: Vermont's gas utility signed a first community geothermal deal, cutting energy use in affordable homes by 40%. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Ask your energy supplier whether heat pump or geothermal schemes are offered where you live. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
item.description: Chemical traces of blood have survived 115 million years inside dinosaur bones. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: What went right this week: the good news that matters
item.description: A weekly roundup: nature restored at scale, Barbados ends HIV passing to babies, cleaner fuels advance. Source: Positive News.

item.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
item.description: Four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy people at genetic risk of Alzheimer's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The butterfly effect: a brighter way to make paint?
item.description: Researchers are learning from butterfly wings to make bright paints without harmful chemical pigments. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana guest ranch, autistic adults work as concierges, guides, wranglers and cooks. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
item.description: Scientists found a hidden immune defence that shields healthy cells from inflammation, ending a 30-year puzzle. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Personalized brain therapy hits 68 percent remission for PTSD
item.description: A newly FDA-cleared personalised brain therapy brought 68% of PTSD patients in trials into remission. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: If PTSD affects you or someone close, ask a doctor about newer treatment options. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Who needs a golden ticket? The race to future-proof chocolate
item.description: A student made chocolate from cocoa grown in England, testing varieties that could cope with a warming climate. Evidence: Early research. Source: Positive News.

item.title: Maya Higa built a wildlife sanctuary on Twitch, funded by the people who watch it
item.description: Streamer Maya Higa built a wildlife sanctuary funded by the viewers who watch its animals online. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: What if we stop treating social care like a service? This village shows the way
item.description: An English village runs its own social care through shared living and neighbours looking after each other. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Ask an older neighbour if they would like a hand with shopping or a lift this week. Source: Positive News.

item.title: Scientists identify two overlooked skills that predict reading success
item.description: A large study finds sound skills, not intelligence, best predict children's reading, showing where help works. How you can help: Play rhyming and sound games with young children to build early reading skills. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
item.description: All five building blocks of DNA and RNA were found in pristine samples from the asteroid Ryugu. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
item.description: An experimental drug rejuvenated liver cells in aged rats and halved an Alzheimer's-linked protein. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
item.description: IceCube, buried in Antarctic ice, is catching neutrinos 10 billion times more energetic than those from the Sun. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: What went right this week: renewed hope for the Brazilian Amazon, plus more
item.description: A weekly roundup: renewed hope for the Amazon, a promising skin cancer vaccine, and a UK nicotine loophole closed. Source: Positive News.

item.title: The Student Exchange Program That Never Leaves the U.S.
item.description: A US exchange programme sends students to live with families in other regions to bridge divides at home. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Smartphones, ancient tracking skills and a future for desert lions
item.description: Namibian rangers pair phone alerts with tracking skills so farmers and recovering desert lions can share the land. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Positive News.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding community through farming, like a hazelnut farm in North Carolina. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants so its famous Palm House can be restored for decades to come. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer
item.description: A tail bone kept in a drawer since 1985 is the first dinosaur bone identified from Antarctica. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
